items.title: Who takes the knowledge exam
items.simple: You take the knowledge exam on a computer. You skip it only with a valid license from a place on this list. The list: another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, Republic of Korea.
items.official: You will need to take the knowledge exam if you do not hold a valid driver's license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, or the Republic of Korea. The two-part knowledge exam is given on a computer. Exam questions are taken from information in this manual.

items.title: Under 18: wait 15 days
items.simple: Under 18 and failed the knowledge exam? You must wait 15 full days to try again. Fail on January 1? Your earliest retake is January 17.
items.official: If you fail the exam and you are under age 18, by law you must wait a full 15 days before you can retake the exam. For example, if you fail the exam on January 1, the earliest you can take the exam again is January 17.
items.mnemonic: Under 18? Fail, then wait 15. Fail on the 1st, retry on the 17th.

items.title: One try per business day
items.simple: You can take the knowledge exam only once per business day. The road skills test works the same way. One try per business day.
items.official: The exam may be taken only once per business day. [Road skills test:] The test may be taken only once per business day.
items.mnemonic: One day, one try.

items.title: Audio, languages, no translators
items.simple: You can listen to an audio version of the exam. It comes in many languages and American Sign Language. So you may not use a translator for those languages. Need special help? Tell a DMV staff member.
items.official: An audio version of the exam is available and the exam is offered in many different languages and American Sign Language. Therefore, translators may not be used for tests in offered languages. Customers with special needs or who require special help with applications or testing should tell a DMV staff member at any DMV location.

items.title: Three fails: classroom driver ed
items.simple: Failed the knowledge exam three times? You cannot take it a fourth time yet. First, finish and pass the classroom part of driver education.
items.official: If you fail the knowledge exam three times, you will not be able to take it a fourth time until you complete and pass the classroom component of driver education.
items.mnemonic: Three strikes, back to class.

items.title: The 8-hour manual course
items.simple: After three fails, you may have another choice: an 8-hour course on this manual. Take it at a driving school or online, after your third fail. Under 18? Finish classroom driver ed first.
items.official: You may have the option of completing an 8-hour course based on the Virginia Driver's Manual and approved by DMV exclusively for satisfying the three-times-failure requirement. This course is available at a driver training school and online. Customers younger than 18 may complete the course if they have previously completed the classroom component of driver education. The completion date must be after the date that you failed the knowledge exam the third time.
items.mnemonic: Three fails? Eight hours.

items.title: Exam rules: no help, no phone
items.simple: During the exam, you cannot get help or help someone else. You cannot get or give test questions or answers. You cannot use a cell phone.
items.official: When testing, you cannot: get help while taking the exam; help another person taking the exam; try to get test questions or answers before the exam; give another person exam questions or answers; use a cell phone during the exam.
items.mnemonic: Just you and the screen. No help, no phone.

items.title: Who takes the road test
items.simple: You must take the road skills test. You skip it only with a valid license from a place on this list. The list: another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, Republic of Korea, Taiwan.
items.official: You will need to take the road skills test if you do not hold a valid driver's license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea, or Taiwan.
items.mnemonic: Road test skip list = exam skip list + Taiwan.

items.title: Road test: bring a safe car
items.simple: You bring the car for the road test. It cannot be an autocycle. It needs a valid inspection sticker, plates and registration. Brakes, belts, horn, lights, signals, mirrors and speedometer must all work.
items.official: You must provide a vehicle for the road skills test (cannot be taken in an autocycle). The vehicle must have a valid safety inspection sticker, license plates, registration card and decals, working brakes, safety belts, horn, lights, turn signals, mirrors and speedometer.

items.title: Driver ed papers or checklist
items.simple: For the road test, show a driver ed completion certificate. Or fill out a behind-the-wheel checklist. On it, a licensed driver says they practiced with you. They also say you followed all permit rules.
items.official: The DMV examiner will require that you either present an acceptable driver's education certificate of completion, or complete a behind-the-wheel checklist (DMV form CSMA 19). A licensed driver will need to certify on the form that he/she has been with you while you practiced the driving tasks and that you have complied with all requirements for learner's permit holders.

items.title: Under 18: test in driver ed
items.simple: Under 18? Your road skills test is part of your driver education course. A public, private or commercial driving school gives it.
items.official: For applicants under 18, the road skills test will be given as part of the driver education course taken at a public, private or commercial driving school.

items.title: 18+: 60-day permit or driver ed
items.simple: Age 18 or older? Before your first road test, hold your learner's permit for 60 days. Or finish driver ed at an approved school. With driver ed, the school gives the test. Otherwise, DMV does.
items.official: Applicants age 18 or older must hold the learner's permit for 60 days prior to the first road skills test or complete a course of driver's education at a driver training school approved by DMV or the Department of Education. For applicants who choose driver's education, the road skills test will be administered by the driver training school. For those who opt to hold a learner's permit for 60 days, the road skills test will be given by a DMV staff member.
items.mnemonic: 18 and up: 60 days or driver ed.

items.title: Failed road test: wait 2 days
items.simple: Failed the road skills test? Wait two days to try again. Failed it at DMV three times? First pass the in-car part of driver ed.
items.official: If you fail the road skills test, you must wait two days to take it again. If you fail the road skills test at DMV three times, you will not be able to take it a fourth time until you complete and pass the in-vehicle part of driver education at a driver training school approved by DMV or the Department of Education.
items.mnemonic: Road test fail: wait 2. Exam fail under 18: wait 15.

items.title: Vision screening for everyone
items.simple: Your tests always include a vision screening. You look into a machine and read letters or numbers. It is not a medical exam. If you fail, you may need to see an eye care professional.
items.official: Tests will include a vision screening and may include a two-part knowledge exam and a road skills test. A DMV representative will tell you which tests you need to take. A DMV staff member will ask you to look into a machine and read a series of letters or numbers. The vision screening is not a medical exam. If you fail the vision screening, you may be asked to visit an eye care professional.

items.title: Restriction C: wear your glasses
items.simple: Need glasses or contacts to pass the vision screening? Then you must wear them every time you drive. Your license shows the letter C for this.
items.official: If you need to wear glasses or contact lenses to pass the vision screening, you must wear them when you drive. Your license will display a C for this restriction. To have this restriction removed after having laser surgery to correct your vision, you must visit a DMV customer service center and pass the vision screening without wearing glasses or contact lenses or submit a Vision Screening Report (MED 4).
items.mnemonic: C on your card? Glasses on your face.

items.title: No limits: 20/40 and 110
items.simple: Want a license with no vision limits? You need 20/40 vision or better in one or both eyes. You also need 110 degrees or more of side vision.
items.official: Driver's license - unrestricted: 20/40 or better vision in one or both eyes, and 110 degrees, or better, horizontal vision in one or both eyes.
items.mnemonic: Full license: 20/40 and 110.

items.title: Daylight only: 20/70 and 70
items.simple: A daylight-only license needs 20/70 vision or better. You also need 70 degrees or more of side vision. Only one eye sees? You need 30 degrees toward your nose and 40 toward your temple.
items.official: Driving - restricted to daylight hours only: 20/70 or better vision in one or both eyes, and 70 degrees, or better, horizontal vision. If you have vision in only one eye, you must have horizontal vision of at least 30 degrees or better when looking toward your nose and 40 degrees or better when looking toward your temple.
items.mnemonic: 70 and 70: daylight only. One eye: nose 30, temple 40. Numbers grow as you look out.

items.title: Daylight hours: half-hour rule
items.simple: Have a daylight-only license? Start driving a half hour after sunrise. Stop driving a half hour before sunset. Never drive outside those times.
items.official: A daylight driving only restricted license permits you to drive only during the period of time beginning a half-hour after sunrise and ending a half-hour before sunset.
items.mnemonic: Sunrise plus a half hour. Sunset minus a half hour.

items.title: Always carry your license
items.simple: Whenever you drive, carry your valid driver's license or learner's permit with you. Misusing your license or permit is illegal. You could be fined, jailed or lose your license.
items.official: Whenever you drive, you must carry a valid driver's license or learner's permit with you. Any misuse of your driver's license or learner's permit is illegal. You could be fined, sentenced to jail, or your license may be suspended.

items.title: Permit: who rides with you
items.simple: Driving with a learner's permit? A licensed driver 21 or older must sit in the front passenger seat. Age 18 to 20 is OK only for a brother, sister or legal guardian.
items.official: A learner's permit allows you to operate a motor vehicle when a licensed driver at least 21 years of age is seated in the front passenger seat. The driver with you must hold a valid driver's license, be alert and able to assist you while you are driving. The licensed driver with you may be age 18, 19, or 20 if he or she is your legal guardian, brother, sister, half-brother, half-sister, step brother or stepsister.
items.mnemonic: Permit pal: 21 up, or a sibling or guardian 18 up.

items.title: Age 19+: permit 60 days
items.simple: Are you 19 or older? Hold your learner's permit for 60 days before you apply for a license. Or show a driver ed completion certificate instead.
items.official: If you are age 19 or older, you must hold a learner's permit for 60 days, or present a driver's education certificate of completion to apply for a driver's license.
items.mnemonic: 19 and up: 60 days or a certificate.

items.title: Regular license: under 26,001 lbs
items.simple: A regular driver's license lets you drive cars. It also covers small trucks under 26,001 pounds. The truck must be one that does not need a CDL.
items.official: A driver's license allows you to operate any vehicle or small truck less than 26,001 pounds that is exempt from commercial driver's license (CDL) requirements.

items.title: CDL for big vehicles
items.simple: Big vehicles need a commercial driver's license (CDL). That means tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tank vehicles and hazardous materials vehicles. School buses for 16 or more people need one too. Count the driver.
items.official: A commercial driver's license (CDL) allows you to operate tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tank vehicles, school buses for 16 or more occupants (including the driver), or vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

items.title: 15-person school bus endorsement
items.simple: A school bus built for 15 people, counting the driver, does not need a CDL. But you must pass the commercial driver and school bus tests. Then you get a school bus endorsement.
items.official: If you wish to operate a school bus designed to carry 15 occupants (including the driver), you do not need to obtain a commercial driver's license. However, you will need to take the commercial driver and school bus tests to obtain the school bus endorsement on your driver's license. You will be restricted to driving a bus designed to carry 15 occupants (including the driver).
items.mnemonic: 15 people: endorsement. 16 or more: CDL.

items.title: International license is not a license
items.simple: An international driver's license is not a real license. It does not let you drive. It is only a translation of your real license for travel outside the U.S.
items.official: An international driver's license is not a valid driver's license and does not allow you to drive. It is only a foreign translation of your existing valid driver's license to be used when you are traveling outside of the U.S. These permits are issued by your local AAA, except to persons whose driving privilege is suspended or revoked. If you are visiting the U.S. from a foreign country, you may drive using your driver's license issued by your home country, accompanied by a translation. International driver's licenses marketed by private sector businesses are not valid. Sale of any document claiming to be a driver's license is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

items.title: License by mail; move in 30
items.simple: Your new license comes in the mail, not at the DMV office. If you move, tell DMV within 30 days. The post office will not forward your license.
items.official: You will receive your new driver's license in the mail. For security, DMV does not issue licenses in customer service centers. If you move, you are required to notify DMV within 30 days. The postal service will not forward your license to another address. If DMV does not have your correct address, the postal service will return the license to DMV.
items.mnemonic: Move? Tell DMV in 30.

items.title: New resident: license in 60 days
items.simple: Just moved to Virginia and you drive? Get a Virginia driver's license within 60 days of moving here.
items.official: If you are a new Virginia resident and drive, you must obtain a Virginia driver's license within 60 days of moving here.
items.mnemonic: New here: plates in 30, license in 60.

items.title: Title, register, plates: 30 days
items.simple: Moved to Virginia? Title and register your vehicle and get Virginia license plates within 30 days. Your city or county may also need you to register it there.
items.official: Title and register your vehicle and obtain Virginia license plates within 30 days of moving to Virginia. You must also register your vehicle in your locality, if required. Check with your city or county government.
items.mnemonic: New here: plates in 30, license in 60.

items.title: Two plates and the card
items.simple: Put license plates on the front and back of your car. Put the decals showing the month and year your registration ends on the plates. Keep your registration card with you when you drive.
items.official: License plates must be displayed on the front and rear of the vehicle. Decals indicating the month and year that the registration expires must be placed in the designated areas on the plates (except for vehicles displaying permanent plates). You must have the vehicle registration card with you when operating the vehicle.
items.mnemonic: Plates front and back. Card in the car.

items.title: Safety inspection every year
items.simple: Your vehicle must pass a safety inspection every year. It must show a valid inspection sticker. Some places also require an emissions inspection.
items.official: Your vehicle must pass an annual vehicle safety inspection and display a valid safety inspection sticker. In certain localities, your vehicle also must pass an emissions inspection.

items.title: The penny tread test
items.simple: Check your tires every month, or before a long trip, with a penny. Put Lincoln's head into a tread groove. If tread covers part of his head, your tread is safe.
items.official: Once every month, or before a long road trip, check your tires for wear and damage problems by using the penny test. Select a point on your tire where the tread appears to be lowest and place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves. If any part of Lincoln's head is covered by the tread, you're driving with the safe amount of tread. If your tread gets below that, your car's ability to grip the road in adverse conditions is greatly reduced.
items.mnemonic: Lincoln's head hidden a bit? Tread is fit.

items.title: Tire pressure: check the door jamb
items.simple: Before you get in the car, check tire pressure with a tire pressure gauge. The right PSI is in your owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb.
items.official: Prior to entering the vehicle, check tire pressure using a tire pressure gauge. The recommended PSI (pounds per square inch) is located in the vehicle owner's manual or the driver's side door jamb of the vehicle.
items.mnemonic: Penny for tread. Gauge for air.

items.title: Register to vote at DMV
items.simple: You can apply to register to vote at any DMV office. You can also change your voter address there. You must be a U.S. citizen and live in Virginia. You must be 18 by the next general election.
items.official: You may apply to register to vote or to change your voter registration mailing address at any DMV office. To apply to register to vote in Virginia, you must be a U.S. citizen, a resident of Virginia, and be at least 18 years old by the next general election. You must have had your voting rights restored by a circuit court if you have been convicted of a felony or if you have been declared mentally incompetent.

items.title: Organ donor: check yes
items.simple: Want to be an organ, eye and tissue donor? Check yes on your license, permit or ID card application. Under 18? Your parents or guardians make the final choice.
items.official: To sign up to be a donor, check yes on your driver's license, learners permit, or ID card application. If you are age 18 or older, your registered decision to be a donor will be honored. If you are under age 18, you can indicate your wishes to donate by checking yes; by law, your parents and guardians must make the final decision.

questions.prompt: If you are under 18 and fail the knowledge exam, you must wait how long before you retake it?
questions.explain: By law, if you are under 18 you must wait a full 15 days to retake the exam.

questions.prompt: You are 17 and fail the knowledge exam on January 1. The earliest you can take it again is:
questions.explain: Under 18, you wait a full 15 days, so a January 1 fail means January 17 at the earliest.

questions.prompt: The 15-day wait to retake a failed knowledge exam applies to people:
questions.explain: The full 15-day wait is the law for people under age 18.

questions.prompt: The knowledge exam may be taken:
choices: Up to three times a day
As many times as you want in one day
questions.explain: The knowledge exam may be taken only once per business day.

questions.prompt: How often may you take the road skills test?
choices: Up to three times a day
questions.explain: The road skills test may be taken only once per business day.

questions.prompt: Translators may not be used for the knowledge exam because:
choices: The exam is only given in English
The exam is offered in many languages and American Sign Language
questions.explain: The exam comes in many languages and ASL, so translators may not be used.

questions.prompt: Which is available for the knowledge exam?
questions.explain: An audio version of the exam is available.

questions.prompt: If you need special help with testing, you should:
choices: Bring a friend to help you
questions.explain: Customers who need special help with testing should tell a DMV staff member.

questions.prompt: If you fail the knowledge exam three times, before you can take it a fourth time you must:
choices: Complete and pass the classroom component of driver education
Hold a learner's permit for 60 days
questions.explain: After three failures, you must complete and pass classroom driver education first.

questions.prompt: After how many failed knowledge exams must you pass classroom driver education before trying again?
questions.explain: Three failed knowledge exams means you must complete classroom driver education first.

questions.prompt: The DMV-approved course for people who fail the knowledge exam three times lasts:
questions.explain: The course based on the Virginia Driver's Manual is 8 hours long.

questions.prompt: To take the 8-hour driver's manual course, a customer under 18 must first:
choices: Hold a learner's permit for 60 days
Have completed the classroom component of driver education
questions.explain: Customers younger than 18 must have completed classroom driver education first.

questions.prompt: The 8-hour driver's manual course must be completed:
choices: Within 15 days of your first exam
After the date you failed the knowledge exam the third time
questions.explain: The course completion date must be after your third failed knowledge exam.

questions.prompt: While taking the knowledge exam, you cannot:
questions.explain: During the exam you cannot get help, give help, or use a cell phone.

questions.prompt: Which of these is allowed when you take the knowledge exam?
choices: Using the audio version of the exam
Getting exam answers before the exam
questions.explain: The audio version is allowed, but phones, early answers and helping others are not.

questions.prompt: Giving another person exam questions or answers is:
questions.explain: You cannot give another person exam questions or answers.

questions.prompt: You must take a road skills test if you do not hold a valid driver's license from:
choices: Another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea or Taiwan
questions.explain: The road skills test is needed unless you hold a valid license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea or Taiwan.

questions.prompt: Someone getting their very first driver's license will take:
choices: A vision screening, knowledge exam and road skills test
questions.explain: Everyone gets a vision screening, and a first-time driver also takes the knowledge exam and road test.

questions.prompt: A valid driver's license from which place lets you skip the road skills test, but not the knowledge exam?
questions.explain: Taiwan is on the road skills test list but not on the knowledge exam list.

questions.prompt: The vehicle you use for the road skills test must have:
questions.explain: The road test vehicle needs a valid inspection sticker, plates, registration, and working safety equipment.

questions.prompt: The road skills test cannot be taken in:
choices: A car with a valid inspection sticker
questions.explain: You must provide a vehicle, and it cannot be an autocycle.

questions.prompt: To take the road skills test, you must present a driver education certificate of completion or:
choices: A behind-the-wheel checklist signed by a licensed driver
questions.explain: The examiner requires a driver ed certificate or a behind-the-wheel checklist.

questions.prompt: On the behind-the-wheel checklist, a licensed driver certifies that:
choices: They were with you while you practiced the driving tasks
You have never had a ticket
questions.explain: The licensed driver certifies they were with you while you practiced and you followed permit rules.

questions.prompt: For applicants under 18, the road skills test is given:
choices: As part of the driver education course
questions.explain: Under 18, the road test is part of driver education at a public, private or commercial school.

questions.prompt: Which applicants take the road skills test as part of a driver education course?
questions.explain: For applicants under 18, the road skills test is part of driver education.

questions.prompt: If you are 18 or older, before your first road skills test you must:
choices: Hold a learner's permit for 30 days
Hold a learner's permit for 60 days or complete driver education
questions.explain: Age 18 or older: hold the permit 60 days or complete driver education first.

questions.prompt: An adult who completes driver education at an approved driver training school takes the road skills test from:
questions.explain: For adults who choose driver education, the driver training school gives the road test.

questions.prompt: If you are 18 or older and do not take driver education, how long must you hold a learner's permit before your first road skills test?
questions.explain: Applicants 18 or older must hold the permit 60 days or complete driver education.

questions.prompt: If you fail the road skills test, you must wait how long before taking it again?
questions.explain: If you fail the road skills test, you must wait two days to take it again.

questions.prompt: After failing the road skills test at DMV three times, before a fourth try you must:
choices: Complete and pass the in-vehicle part of driver education
questions.explain: Three road test failures at DMV means you must pass in-vehicle driver education first.

questions.prompt: After three failed road skills tests at DMV, the in-vehicle part of driver education must be completed:
choices: Before your first road skills test
After the date you failed the road skills test the third time
Within two days of your third failure
At a DMV customer service center
questions.explain: The in-vehicle completion date must be after your third failed road skills test.

questions.prompt: The DMV vision screening:
questions.explain: The vision screening is not a medical exam; it checks if you meet Virginia's standards.

questions.prompt: During the vision screening, you will:
choices: Read a page of the manual aloud
Look into a machine and read letters or numbers
Get eye drops from a doctor
questions.explain: A DMV staff member asks you to look into a machine and read letters or numbers.

questions.prompt: If you fail the vision screening, you may be asked to:
choices: Take the road skills test twice
questions.explain: If you fail the vision screening, you may be asked to visit an eye care professional.

questions.prompt: Who tells you which DMV tests you need to take?
questions.explain: Tests include a vision screening, and a DMV representative tells you which tests you need.

questions.prompt: If you need glasses to pass the vision screening, your license will show:
questions.explain: Needing glasses or contacts to pass puts a C restriction on your license.

questions.prompt: If your license has a C restriction, you must:
choices: Wear your glasses or contact lenses when you drive
Drive only with a licensed driver age 21 or older
questions.explain: A C restriction means you must wear glasses or contacts when you drive.

questions.prompt: To remove a glasses restriction after laser eye surgery, you must:
choices: Pass DMV's vision screening without glasses or contacts, or submit a Vision Screening Report
Take the road skills test again
questions.explain: After laser surgery, pass the screening without glasses or contacts, or submit a Vision Screening Report (MED 4).

questions.prompt: To get an unrestricted driver's license, you need vision of:
questions.explain: An unrestricted license needs 20/40 or better vision in one or both eyes.

questions.prompt: For an unrestricted license, you need horizontal vision of at least:
questions.explain: An unrestricted license needs 110 degrees or better of horizontal vision.

questions.prompt: A driver with 20/40 vision and 110 degrees of horizontal vision may get:
questions.explain: 20/40 vision and 110 degrees horizontal vision meet the unrestricted standard.

questions.prompt: A driver with 20/70 vision and 70 degrees of horizontal vision may be restricted to:
questions.explain: 20/70 vision and 70 degrees horizontal vision meet the daylight-only standard.

questions.prompt: For a license restricted to daylight driving, you need vision of:
questions.explain: Daylight-only driving needs 20/70 or better vision in one or both eyes.

questions.prompt: If you have vision in only one eye, a daylight-only license requires horizontal vision of at least:
choices: 40 degrees toward your nose and 30 degrees toward your temple
70 degrees toward your nose and 110 degrees toward your temple
30 degrees toward your nose and 40 degrees toward your temple
10 degrees toward your nose and 20 degrees toward your temple
questions.explain: With one eye, you need 30 degrees toward your nose and 40 degrees toward your temple.

questions.prompt: A daylight-only restricted license lets you drive:
choices: From a half hour after sunrise until a half hour before sunset
From one hour after sunrise until one hour before sunset
From a half hour before sunrise until a half hour after sunset
questions.explain: Daylight-only means from a half hour after sunrise to a half hour before sunset.

questions.prompt: With a daylight-only license, you must finish driving by:
questions.explain: A daylight-only license ends your driving a half hour before sunset.

questions.prompt: Whenever you drive, you must carry:
choices: A valid driver's license or learner's permit
questions.explain: You must carry a valid driver's license or learner's permit whenever you drive.

questions.prompt: Misuse of your driver's license or learner's permit can result in:
questions.explain: Misusing your license or permit is illegal and can bring a fine, jail, or suspension.

questions.prompt: A learner's permit allows you to drive when a licensed driver at least how old is in the front passenger seat?
questions.explain: The licensed driver with you must be at least 21, unless a sibling or legal guardian age 18 to 20.

questions.prompt: When you drive with a learner's permit, the licensed driver with you must:
choices: Sit in the front passenger seat
Be alert and able to help you
questions.explain: The supervising driver must hold a valid license, sit in front, and be alert and able to help.

questions.prompt: A licensed driver age 18, 19 or 20 may supervise your learner's permit driving only if they are your:
questions.explain: A supervisor age 18 to 20 must be your legal guardian, brother, sister, half-sibling or stepsibling.

questions.prompt: Your licensed 19-year-old stepbrother sits in the front passenger seat. With a learner's permit, you:
choices: May drive only in parking lots
questions.explain: A licensed stepbrother age 18 to 20 may be your supervising driver.

questions.prompt: If you are 19 or older, to apply for a driver's license you must hold a learner's permit for 60 days or:
choices: Present a driver's education certificate of completion
Bring a note from a parent
questions.explain: Age 19 or older: hold the permit 60 days or show a driver ed certificate.

questions.prompt: How long must a 19-year-old without driver education hold a learner's permit before applying for a license?
questions.explain: If you are 19 or older, you must hold a learner's permit for 60 days.

questions.prompt: A regular driver's license allows you to drive a small truck that weighs less than:
questions.explain: A driver's license covers small trucks less than 26,001 pounds that do not need a CDL.

questions.prompt: Which vehicle can you drive with a regular Virginia driver's license?
questions.explain: Tractor-trailers, tank vehicles and hazardous materials vehicles need a CDL.

questions.prompt: A commercial driver's license (CDL) is needed to drive:
questions.explain: A CDL covers tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tank vehicles, big school buses and hazardous materials.

questions.prompt: A CDL is needed to drive a school bus that carries how many occupants, including the driver?
questions.explain: School buses for 16 or more occupants, including the driver, need a CDL.

questions.prompt: To drive a school bus designed to carry 15 occupants including the driver, you need:
choices: A school bus endorsement on your driver's license
questions.explain: A 15-occupant school bus needs a school bus endorsement, not a CDL.

questions.prompt: To get a school bus endorsement, you must pass:
choices: The commercial driver and school bus tests
questions.explain: You take the commercial driver and school bus tests to get the endorsement.

questions.prompt: A school bus endorsement restricts you to buses designed to carry:
questions.explain: The endorsement limits you to a bus designed to carry 15 occupants, including the driver.

questions.prompt: An international driver's license:
choices: Lets you drive without any other license
Is not a valid driver's license
questions.explain: An international driver's license is only a translation of your real license.

questions.prompt: A visitor from a foreign country may drive in the U.S. using:
choices: Their home country driver's license with a translation
An international license bought from a private business
questions.explain: Visitors may drive with their home country license, accompanied by a translation.

questions.prompt: Selling any document that claims to be a driver's license is:
questions.explain: Sale of any document claiming to be a driver's license is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

questions.prompt: You will receive your new driver's license:
choices: At the DMV customer service center that day
questions.explain: For security, DMV mails licenses and does not issue them in customer service centers.

questions.prompt: If you move, you must notify DMV within:
questions.explain: If you move, you are required to notify DMV within 30 days.

questions.prompt: If DMV does not have your correct address, your new license will be:
choices: Returned to DMV by the postal service
questions.explain: The postal service will not forward your license, so it goes back to DMV.

questions.prompt: New Virginia residents who drive must get a Virginia driver's license within:
questions.explain: New residents must obtain a Virginia driver's license within 60 days of moving here.

questions.prompt: Which is true for new Virginia residents?
choices: Get a license within 60 days; title, register and get plates within 30 days
Get a license within 30 days; get plates within 60 days
Get a license and plates within one year
Get a license and plates within 10 days
questions.explain: New residents get a license within 60 days and title, register and get plates within 30 days.

questions.prompt: After moving to Virginia, you must title and register your vehicle and get Virginia plates within:
questions.explain: Title, register and get Virginia license plates within 30 days of moving to Virginia.

questions.prompt: Within 30 days of moving to Virginia, you must:
choices: Title and register your vehicle and get Virginia license plates
Sign up as an organ donor
questions.explain: New residents must title, register and get Virginia plates within 30 days.

questions.prompt: License plates must be displayed:
choices: On the front and rear of the vehicle
questions.explain: Virginia license plates go on the front and rear of the vehicle.

questions.prompt: When you drive, you must have with you:
questions.explain: You must have the vehicle registration card with you when you drive.

questions.prompt: The decals on your license plates show:
choices: The month and year the registration expires
questions.explain: Decals show the month and year the registration expires.

questions.prompt: In Virginia, your vehicle must pass a safety inspection:
questions.explain: Virginia requires an annual vehicle safety inspection.

questions.prompt: After it passes safety inspection, your vehicle must display:
questions.explain: Your vehicle must display a valid safety inspection sticker.

questions.prompt: In certain localities, your vehicle must also pass:
questions.explain: Some localities also require an emissions inspection.

questions.prompt: In the penny test, if any part of Lincoln's head is covered by the tread:
choices: You have a safe amount of tread
Your tires need replacing right away
Your tire pressure is too low
Your tires have too much air
questions.explain: If tread covers any part of Lincoln's head, you are driving with a safe amount of tread.

questions.prompt: How often should you check your tires with the penny test?
choices: Once every month, or before a long road trip
Only when a tire looks flat
questions.explain: Check your tires with the penny test once every month or before a long road trip.

questions.prompt: If your tire tread gets too low:
choices: Your car's ability to grip the road in bad conditions is greatly reduced
Your tires grip better in rain
questions.explain: Low tread greatly reduces your car's grip on the road in adverse conditions.

questions.prompt: The recommended tire pressure (PSI) for your vehicle is found:
choices: In the owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb
questions.explain: Recommended PSI is in the owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb.

questions.prompt: To check your tire pressure, use:
questions.explain: Check tire pressure with a tire pressure gauge before entering the vehicle.

questions.prompt: To apply to register to vote in Virginia, you must:
choices: Be at least 18 by the next general election
questions.explain: Voters must be U.S. citizens, Virginia residents, and 18 by the next general election.

questions.prompt: You may apply to register to vote or change your voter mailing address:
questions.explain: You may apply to register to vote or change your voter address at any DMV office.

questions.prompt: If you have been convicted of a felony, to register to vote in Virginia you must first:
choices: Have your voting rights restored by a circuit court
questions.explain: After a felony conviction, a circuit court must restore your voting rights before you can register.

questions.prompt: To sign up as an organ, eye and tissue donor, you can:
choices: Check yes on your driver's license, permit or ID card application
Write it on your license plate
Do nothing; everyone is signed up
questions.explain: Check yes on your license, permit or ID card application to be a donor.

questions.prompt: If you are under 18 and check yes to be a donor:
choices: Your parents or guardians make the final decision
It does not count at all
questions.explain: By law, parents and guardians make the final decision for donors under 18.

questions.prompt: If you are 18 or older, your registered decision to be a donor will be:
questions.explain: At 18 or older, your registered decision to be a donor will be honored.
